title: Immunolocalization and Immunoblotting of PI3K Signaling in Chick Embryos
author: Gheyas, Menko
materials: Pierce ECL plus western blotting substrate

steps.title: Obtain and incubate fertilized eggs
steps.instruction: Acquire fertilized white leghorn chicken eggs (e.g., from Poultry Futures or Charles River) and place them in a GQF Digital Sportsman Cabinet set to 37 °C with 45‑55 % humidity until needed.

steps.title: Prepare lens organ cultures
steps.instruction: Determine the embryonic stage (E8‑E15) for lens organ culture, reconstitute signaling pathway inhibitors, and select target antibodies with appropriate dilutions.

steps.title: Fix lenses for immunolocalization
steps.instruction: Wash lenses twice with PBS in a 48‑well plate, then add 0.5 mL per well of 4 % paraformaldehyde (prepared by diluting 16 % stock in PBS) and incubate 2 h at 4 °C.

steps.title: Cryoprotect lenses
steps.instruction: Wash lenses twice with PBS, then add 0.5 mL per well of 30 % sucrose in PBS and incubate 24 h at 4 °C (lenses can be stored in sucrose up to 1 month).

steps.title: Microdissect lenses
steps.instruction: Using a dissecting microscope and forceps, separate each lens into three fractions – epithelium, cortical fiber cells, and nuclear fiber cells – and place each fraction on ice in a 0.5 mL microfuge tube containing 1‑2 µL Imidazole Buffer with protease/phosphatase inhibitors (1:100). Combine like fractions from multiple lenses; samples may be stored at –80 °C.

substeps.instruction: Place lens on lid of a 100 mm petri dish.
Create a shallow puncture in the anterior epithelium, widen the tear, and pull the epithelium away.
Remove cortical fibers (FP) from the central nuclear fibers (FC).

steps.title: Extract protein from fractions
steps.instruction: Add 2X OG/T extraction buffer in a volume equal to the Imidazole Buffer in each tube, homogenize with a disposable plastic pestle (~30 s) until no tissue pieces remain, incubate on ice 15 min, centrifuge 5 min at 15 000 × g, and transfer the supernatant to a new tube (store at –80 °C if needed).

steps.title: Determine protein concentration (BCA assay)
steps.instruction: Dilute epithelial samples 1:20 and fiber samples 1:80 in Imidazole Buffer; prepare a BSA standard curve (0.025‑2 mg/mL); load 5 µL of standards, samples, and blank (Imidazole Buffer) in triplicate into a 96‑well plate; add 200 µL of reagents A + B mixed 50:1 to each well; cover and incubate 30 min at 37 °C; read absorbance at 562 nm. Note: 5‑10 lenses yield ~10 µg protein for epithelium and ~15 µg for each fiber fraction.

steps.title: Freeze lenses for sectioning
steps.instruction: Remove lenses from sucrose with forceps, embed each in ~4 mL tissue freezing media placed in a 22 × 22 mm square mold (equatorial epithelium up, anterior/posterior sides left/right), and freeze the mold in a dry‑ice/ethanol bath.

steps.title: Cryosection frozen lenses
steps.instruction: Set a Microm HM 500 cryostat to –25 °C, allow blocks to equilibrate 20 min, then cut sections 20 µm thick (range 6‑20 µm) and mount on microscope slides. Store blocks at –80 °C and sections at –20 °C.

steps.title: Immunostain lens sections
steps.instruction: Select central sections, draw a hydrophobic pen square around each, acclimate sections to 22 °C for ~10 min, then:

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µL Permeabilization Buffer, incubate 30 min at ~22 °C, and remove.
Add 100 µL Block Buffer, incubate 1 h at ~22 °C, and remove.
Incubate with primary antibodies diluted in Block Buffer (37 °C 3 h or 4 °C ~16 h), wash PBS 5 min ×3.
Incubate with secondary antibody + DAPI (1:1000) in Block Buffer, 37 °C 2 h, wash PBS 5 min ×3.
Add a drop of ProLong Diamond Antifade, cover with a coverslip.

steps.title: Prepare samples for WES immunoblot
steps.instruction: For each well, combine the sample with 0.6 µL Fluorescent Master Mix and add sample buffer to bring the volume to 3 µL (0.1X from 10X stock); heat 100 °C for 5 min.

steps.title: Load WES plate
steps.instruction: Load 5 µL biotinylated ladder into the first well of the first row, then load 3 µL of each prepared sample into the remaining wells of the first row (24 wells total). Load 10 µL Antibody Diluent II into every well of the second row. Load 10 µL Antibody Diluent II into the first well of the third row (ladder). Load 10 µL diluted primary antibodies into the remaining wells of the third row. Load 10 µL Streptavidin‑HRP into the first well of the fourth row (ladder) and 10 µL secondary antibody into the other fourth‑row wells. Mix luminol and peroxide 1:1 and add 15 µL to each well of the fifth row. Centrifuge the plate at 1000 × g for 5 min. Load 500 µL wash buffer into all wells of rows seven, eight, and nine. Remove the lower seal, place the plate and capillaries into the WES instrument, and run (~3 h). Optimal sample protein amount: 0.005‑3 µg.

steps.title: Prepare samples for traditional Western blot
steps.instruction: Mix each protein sample with an equal volume of 2X Sample Buffer (Novex Tris‑Glycine), heat 10 min at 100 °C, and keep the final volume ≤40 µL (aim for ~50 µg protein per well).

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE gel electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Assemble a Mini‑Cell apparatus with a 4‑12 % (or 8‑16 %) gradient gel, fill with 1X Running Buffer, and run at 80 V until the stacking gel clears, then increase to 120 V until the dye front reaches the bottom (~3 h).

steps.title: Transfer proteins to PVDF membrane
steps.instruction: Cut PVDF to 8 × 8 cm, hydrate in 100 % methanol 10 s, rinse with milliQ water, then assemble the transfer stack (sponge, chromatography paper, gel, PVDF, paper, sponge) in a Hoefer TE22 cassette. Fill the apparatus with 1X Transfer Buffer, run at 280 mA for 210 min at 4 °C (membrane pore size 0.45 µm).

steps.title: Block membrane
steps.instruction: Incubate the PVDF membrane in 5 % milk (10 g powdered milk in 200 mL 1X TBS‑T, pH 7.6, filtered) for 1 h at 22 °C with gentle rocking.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation (Western blot)
steps.instruction: Add primary antibodies diluted in 5 % milk and incubate ~16 h at 4 °C (or as required).

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation (Western blot)
steps.instruction: Add HRP‑conjugated secondary antibody diluted in 5 % milk, incubate 2 h at 22 °C.

steps.title: Detect Western blot signals
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane with TBS‑T for 30 min at 22 °C, incubate with ECL Plus for 5 min, and image the chemiluminescent bands using a FluorChem E&M imager.

steps.title: Acquire confocal images
steps.instruction: Using a Zeiss LSM800, locate the lens section at 5X or 10X, switch to 40X, set optical section thickness (e.g., 0.7 µm) or acquire a full‑thickness z‑stack, adjust laser wavelength and detector gain (up to 800 V) to avoid saturation, set up a tile scan covering the entire section (tile number depends on lens size), acquire images (e.g., 10 × 10 tile, 3 channels, scan speed 7, ~20 min), then process in Zen software (brightness/contrast, channel overlay, intensity measurement, orthogonal projections).

description: Fertilized white leghorn chicken eggs should be acquired from sources such as Poultry Futures (Lilitz, PA) or Charles River (Wilmington, MA) and incubated in a GQF Digital Sportsman Cabinet (egg incubator) which is set to 37°C and humidity between 45%-55% until use. Determine the embryonic stage of interest to prepare the chick embryo lens organ cultures. These cultures can be grown successfully from E8-E15, depending on the particular time of development at which the investigator wishes to examine the impact of inhibiting a signaling pathway. Inhibitors should be purchased and reconstituted prior to beginning this protocol. Antibodies which will be the targets of interest for analysis using the immunolocalization/immunoblotting protocols should be determined, as well as the appropriate antibody dilution. While this protocol is focused on understanding the role of PI3K signaling pathways in the regulation of lens organelle loss, we have used that same approach to examine the role of other pathways.
